Senses.Explanation: Literally, “he is now exactly me.” The line occurs 65 times in 41 allowlisted texts as a quotation from Dongshan Liangjie’s verse after seeing his reflection while crossing water. The surviving verse supplies the indispensable continuation: “I now go alone; everywhere I meet him. He is now exactly me; I am now not him. One must understand in this way to tally with thusness” (我今獨自往，處處得逢渠。渠今正是我，我今不是渠。應須與摩會，方得契如如). Later Caodong records explicitly say “the five ranks of lord and minister all issue from this” (五位君臣都從此出), turn each half into public questions, and criticize proposed uses: Yongjue comments “still separated by one mountain” after the first line, while another master answers a monk’s use of the couplet by asking where the fault lies. The phrase’s Zen-specific identity is this named line in Dongshan’s water-reflection verse and its later deployment as a source line, interview question, and object of criticism. This entry does not resolve the pronouns beyond the verse’s wording.
Senses.Note: The quotation has one corpus-wide identity despite its origin with Dongshan; later masters preserve, question, and criticize it without establishing a different master-specific referent. The paired line “I am now not him” (我今不是渠) is required context, not a second sense.

Occurrences.Kwic: 我今獨自往，處處得逢渠。渠今正是我，我今不是渠。應須與摩會，方得契如如。
渠今正是我，我今不是渠，五位君臣都從此出。
問：「明暗雙機，學人不易。如何是渠今正是我？」師云：「蠱毒之鄉水莫嘗。」
渠今正是我，猶隔一重山；我今不是渠，蹉過知多少？
一僧著語云：「渠今正是我，我今不是渠。」師云：「銜銕負鞍有日在。且道過在甚麼處？試檢點看。」
